summary: Turned away from voting: {poll worker} tells you, or {close tie} beside you, that a voting rule on record means no ordinary ballot today.
realLife: In 1962 the Mississippi sharecropper went with others to register, was failed on the literacy test and was fired by her boss for trying. She went on to help found the Mississippi Freedom Democratic Party.
gates: A voting rule in your state (ID, a roll purge, a moved polling place) that a fact of your household does not meet, such as a recent move or a name change.
Election day or a registration deadline.
weights: How strongly you hold views on the race.
choices: ask to see the rule in writing
go to {clerk}'s office before the polls close

branches.when: it is an older relative who is turned away
branches.then: She asks you to drive her to {clerk}'s office, and whether she votes depends on you.
You must turn a neighbor away under the rule: follow it, offer the provisional ballot, or call {clerk}.
Your employer brings it up at work the next day, and your job is at stake for speaking out.
